name: Crispus (synagogue ruler)
title: First Christian leader of the Corinthian synagogue
summary: Crispus was the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth who came to faith in Jesus Christ through the preaching of the apostle Paul. He and his entire household were baptized, and he became one of the few whom Paul personally baptized. His conversion was significant because it showed that even Jewish religious leaders responded to the gospel.

keyEvents.title: Comes to faith in the Lord
keyEvents.description: Crispus, who was the synagogue ruler in Corinth, came to faith in the Lord along with his entire household. This happened while Paul was preaching in the synagogue.

keyEvents.title: Baptized personally by Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul mentions Crispus as one of the few he personally baptized in Corinth, which highlights his importance as one of the first believers there.

keyEvents.title: Paul's ministry in Corinth
keyEvents.description: Crispus' conversion took place during Paul's stay in Corinth, where the apostle worked together with Aquila and Priscilla and preached in the synagogue every Sabbath.
